feed.title: AI · Models & Assistants — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Can I Vibecode It?
entry.summary: A table testing whether AI can rebuild a thousand-odd apps, with the verdict published. It hands you the exact prompt used, so the result is reproducible.

entry.title: Anthropic Claude
entry.summary: Model versions, context limits and token pricing, with the cost-reducing features — prompt caching, the batch API — laid out side by side.

entry.title: Cohere
entry.summary: Rather than compete on chat, it sits on the retrieval side: its Rerank model reorders candidates returned by vector search and visibly lifts RAG precision.

entry.title: Google AI Studio
entry.summary: A browser surface for testing prompts, setting system instructions and fiddling with temperature. It exports whatever call you just tried as ready code.

entry.title: Google Gemini
entry.summary: Connects straight into Gmail, Drive and YouTube to use your own content as source. That integration is decisive if you live in Google’s ecosystem and irrelevant if you do not.

entry.title: LM Studio
entry.summary: A desktop app for finding GGUF models, downloading them and picking a quantisation level. It tells you upfront which quant fits your RAM; with Ollama you work that out yourself.

entry.title: Meta Llama
entry.summary: Weights are downloadable and run on your own hardware. The licence is not fully OSI-compliant: there is a monthly-active-user threshold for large commercial use — read it before shipping.

entry.title: Microsoft Copilot
entry.summary: Runs embedded in Word, Excel and the Windows shell, so you operate on a document without copying it to a website. The underlying models are OpenAI’s; the difference is the delivery point.

entry.title: Mistral AI
entry.summary: Europe-based provider that ships its small models (7B and below) under Apache-2.0. They fit on a single consumer GPU, which matters when hardware is the constraint.

entry.title: Ollama
entry.summary: Built on llama.cpp; one command pulls and runs a model. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint, so existing client code runs unchanged.

entry.title: Open WebUI
entry.summary: A web front-end for Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, adding multi-user accounts, role management and document upload for RAG. Usually deployed with Docker.

entry.title: OpenAI Platform
entry.summary: API keys, rate limits and billing. Organisation-level quota settings and usage graphs live here too.

entry.title: Phind
entry.summary: Answers developer questions with a code block and source links rather than a page of results. A substitute for trawling Stack Overflow; it falls behind general assistants outside that domain.

entry.title: vLLM
entry.summary: PagedAttention pages the KV cache to use GPU memory efficiently, and continuous batching pushes concurrent-request throughput far past what Ollama manages.

entry.title: Kimi K2.7 Code
entry.summary: Moonshot AI’s code-focused open-weight model — a genuine option if you want a local coding assistant without wiring yourself to a closed API.

entry.title: LocateAnything-3B
entry.summary: A visual grounding model that boxes an object in an image from a text description. Unlike classification it is not tied to a predefined label set.

entry.title: Hugging Bay
entry.summary: An alternative browser placing open models side by side with licence and provenance. It publishes SHA-256 hashes for downloads, so integrity is verifiable.

entry.title: Unlimited-OCR
entry.summary: Baidu’s OCR model, extracting text from long multi-column documents with no page ceiling. Markedly better than a classic Tesseract pipeline at preserving tables and layout.

entry.title: OpenAI API Dokümantasyonu
entry.summary: Parameter reference for the Chat Completions, Responses and Realtime endpoints. The primary source for function-calling schemas and streaming behaviour.

entry.title: Google AI for Developers
entry.summary: Developer gateway for the Gemini API and the open-weight Gemma family. The free tier is wide enough to carry a real prototype and asks for no card.

entry.title: Hugging Face
entry.summary: The central repository for models, datasets and Spaces demos. Each model card carries licence, training data and eval results — read that before you download.

entry.title: OpenClaw
entry.summary: A personal assistant that runs on your own machine. It has no UI of its own; it hooks into chat apps you already use, and data never leaves the device.

entry.title: Kimi Claw
entry.summary: A hosted layer on OpenClaw adding persistent memory, scheduled tasks and jobs that fire without being asked. For people who do not want to operate their own server.

entry.title: Claude
entry.summary: A 200K-token context window carries long documents and whole codebases. Projects keeps files as persistent context across chats; Artifacts runs output in a side panel.

entry.title: DeepSeek
entry.summary: V3 and R1 weights are downloadable. A mixture-of-experts architecture keeps total parameters high while activating only a slice per token, which is how it delivers reasoning performance at far lower inference cost.

entry.title: ChatGPT
entry.summary: Sandboxed Python execution, image generation, file upload and custom GPTs in one window. The breadth costs it depth — no single capability is best-in-class.

entry.title: NotebookLM
entry.summary: Builds a context limited to the PDFs, docs and links you upload, and refuses to answer outside them. The constraint cuts hallucination; the price is that you cannot ask it general questions.

entry.title: Perplexity
entry.summary: Turns your query into a web search, feeds the retrieved pages to a model, then footnotes each sentence. It is a RAG pipeline: answers rest on live search results, not the model’s memory.
